technical.summary: Strong trend structure (ADX, long-term EMAs bullish) undermined by bearish price action (three black crows, negative CMF, price below short-term MAs), creating conflicting signals unsuitable for high-probability swing entry.

fundamental.summary: SRE shows no fundamental momentum with zero insider activity, no institutional signal, absent government contracts, no lobbying presence, and minimal retail interest; earnings in 9 days present elevated volatility risk with no supporting smart money conviction.

sentiment.summary: Extreme fear (23/100) presents contrarian buy opportunity, but stale congressional data (18+ months old) and absent news sentiment provide no confirmation.

risk.summary: Crisis VIX (421.6), flat yield curve, rising dollar, and earnings in 9 days create a highly adverse macro backdrop for SRE.

debate.key_bull_argument: Long-term trend structure (ADX strong, EMA 50/200 bullish) combined with extreme fear sentiment (23/100) and proximity to support (71.93) offers contrarian entry for mean reversion if macro stabilizes.
debate.key_bear_argument: Bearish price action (three black crows, price below all short-term MAs, negative CMF/MACD), zero fundamental conviction, crisis VIX, earnings volatility in 9 days, and unfavorable macro environment (rising dollar, flat yield curve) make this a high-risk, low-probability swing entry.

decision.entry_rationale: While price sits at support (71.93) and long-term trend structure remains bullish, bearish price action (three black crows, price below all short-term MAs) combined with zero fundamental conviction and crisis macro conditions (VIX 421.6, rising dollar) create unacceptable risk-reward for swing entry.
decision.primary_risk: Earnings volatility in 9 days combined with crisis VIX and unfavorable macro environment could trigger sharp downside break below support with no institutional or smart money backstop.
decision.agent_agreement: strong — all agents aligned on bear case
decision.portfolio_note: Already holding 37 Utilities positions with existing SRE exposure; sector concentration and earnings proximity argue against adding to position.
